Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 1–10:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-al-ṣāffāti ṣaffā﴾: i.e., the angels who line themselves up in prayer, and their wings in the air.

﴿Fa-al-zājirāti zajrā﴾: i.e., the angels who drive the clouds, that is, drive them wherever Allah permits.

﴿Fa-al-tāliyāti dhikrā﴾: i.e., the groups who recite the Qur'an as a reminder.

﴿Inna ilāhakum la-wāḥid﴾: i.e., your God who is the true object of worship, O people, is indeed One.

﴿Rabbu al-samāwāti wa-al-arḍi wa-mā baynahumā﴾: i.e., He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, that is, their Creator, their Owner, and the Manager of affairs within them.

﴿Wa-rabbu al-mashāriq﴾: i.e., and of the places of sunrise and sunset, for the sun has a rising and a setting every day.

﴿Wa-ḥifẓan min kulli shayṭānin māridin﴾: i.e., and We guarded it with a complete guard from every rebellious devil who has gone beyond obedience.

﴿Lā yassamma'ūna ilā al-mala' al-a'lā﴾: i.e., they do not listen to the angels in the highest heavens.

﴿Wa-yuqdhafūna min kulli jānib, duḥūran﴾: they are pelted with shooting stars from every side of the sky, "duḥūr" meaning driving them away.

﴿'Adhābun wāṣib﴾: i.e., a constant punishment that never leaves them.

﴿Illā man khaṭifa al-khaṭfa﴾: i.e., one who snatches a word from the angels swiftly and flees.

﴿Fa-atbaʿahu shihābun thāqib﴾: i.e., a bright, piercing star that pierces him, burns him, or deranges him, that is, corrupts him.

Meaning of the verses:

The Almighty's words ﴿Wa-al-ṣāffāti ṣaffā﴾ are a divine oath by which He affirms His divinity over His servants. He swears by the lined-up ones, the drivers, and the reciters of the reminder, that is, the Qur'an. Whether we say He swears by these creatures, since it is permissible for Allah to swear by whatever He wills of His creation, while it is forbidden for a servant to swear by other than his Lord; or we say He swears by Himself, meaning "and the Lord of the lined-up ones, etc.," the oath is in either case for the sake of establishing monotheism. This oath follows the custom of people: when someone informs others of a matter about which they doubt its truth, the informant confirms the news with an oath to remove doubt from their souls.

His words ﴿Inna ilāhakum la-wāḥid﴾ are the content of the oath, namely that the God of all humanity is One, Allah, their Creator and Provider, and they have no god other than Him. Whatever other gods they have are false gods; it suffices to show their falsehood that they are idols, images, statues, and crosses that neither hear nor see, and neither benefit nor harm.

His words ﴿Rabbu al-samāwāti wa-al-arḍi wa-mā baynahumā wa-rabbu al-mashāriq﴾ are evidence for the oneness of Allah, for He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, their Owner, and the Manager of affairs within them. He is also the Lord of the places of sunrise and sunset, since each day the sun rises and sets at a specific point. The true God is the Creator of the worlds and their Manager, not the one a man carves with his own hand and then falsely and baselessly calls "my god." Let the polytheists free themselves from the captivity of Satan and worship the Most Merciful.

His words, Exalted is He, ﴿Innā zayyannā al-samā'a al-dunyā bi-zīnati al-kawākib﴾ are signs of power, knowledge, and wisdom: He alone adorned the lowest heaven, that is, the one nearest the earth, with the adornment of the stars, which are bright and luminous.

His words ﴿Wa-ḥifẓan min kulli shayṭānin mārid﴾ mean: and We guarded the heaven with a complete guard from every rebellious devil who has transgressed and rebelled against obedience.

His words ﴿Lā yassamma'ūna ilā al-mala' al-a'lā﴾ mean they do not eavesdrop on the angels in the heaven, so that they cannot convey news of the unseen to their allies among the soothsayers on earth. His words ﴿Wa-yuqdhafūna min kulli jānib﴾ mean those rebellious devils are pelted by the angels from every direction of the heaven, "duḥūran," to drive them off and push them away. His words, Exalted is He, ﴿Wa-lahum 'adhābun wāṣib﴾ mean that for those rebellious devils there is a painful, constant punishment. His words ﴿Illā man khaṭifa al-khaṭfa﴾ mean: except one who snatches a word swiftly, ﴿Fa-atbaʿahu shihābun thāqib﴾ meaning a bright star that pierces him, kills him, burns him, or deranges him, that is, corrupts him. By this, the heaven has been protected by the angels from the entry of devils into it and from eavesdropping. And praise be to Allah.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that Allah swears by some of His creatures, either to indicate their greatness, which implicitly establishes the greatness of their Creator, or to show their excellence, or to draw the servants' attention to the benefits within them.

2- Affirmation of monotheism, that there is no god but Allah.

3- Clarification of the wisdom behind the existence of the stars in the lowest heaven.

4- Clarification that the devils have been prevented from eavesdropping, and that there is no longer room for devils to lie to people after they have been prevented from eavesdropping.

3- Clarification of the wisdom behind the existence of the stars in the lowest heaven.

4- Clarification that the devils have been prevented from eavesdropping, and that there is no longer room for devils to lie to people after they have been prevented from eavesdropping.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verse 11–21:

Explanation of the words:

Fastaftihim (ask them): i.e., question the disbelievers of Makkah, as a means of affirmation and rebuke.

Ahum ashaddu khalqan am man khalaqna (Are they harder to create, or those We have created?): i.e., their own creation in their essence and their return after death, or those whom Allah the Exalted has created: the angels, the heavens, the earth, and all other creatures within them.

Min tinin lazib (of sticky clay): i.e., clay that clings to the hand.

Bal 'ajibta wa yaskhurun (Nay, you are amazed, and they mock): i.e., you are amazed, O Prophet of Allah, at their denial of the Resurrection, while they mock your call to faith in it.

Wa idha dhukkiru la yadhakkarun (And when they are reminded, they do not remember): i.e., when they are admonished, they do not take heed.

Wa idha ra'aw ayatan yastaskhirun (And when they see a sign, they ridicule it): i.e., when they see a proof among the proofs carried by the Qur'anic verses, which establish the Resurrection, Tawhid and Prophethood, they mock, i.e., they deride.

Qul na'am wa antum dakhirun (Say: Yes, and you will be humbled): i.e., say to them, O Our Messenger: Yes, you will be resurrected, and you will be abased and humiliated.

Fa innama hiya zajratun wahidatun (It will be but a single shout): i.e., a cry that drives them, namely the blast of Israfil in the Trumpet, the second blast.

Hadha yawm al-din (This is the Day of Judgment): i.e., the Day of Reckoning and Recompense.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish Tawhid, the Resurrection and the Recompense. Allah's words, "Fastaftihim" (so ask them), mean: question them and seek their answer, by your saying: "Are you harder to create, i.e., in your essence and in your revival after your death, or those whom Allah has created of the angels, the heavens and the earth and what is in them and between them?" The answer is known, namely that the creation of other worlds is harder in creation. So how do they deny the Resurrection on the claim that its occurrence is impossible because of its difficulty? Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We created them from sticky clay﴾, i.e., We created their father Adam from sticky clay that clings to the hand. Then We created them by way of procreation. Will Our re-creating them a second time be beyond Our power? The answer is no. As for His words, ﴿Nay, you are amazed﴾, i.e., at their denial of the Resurrection, because the evidence for its possibility and necessity is clear, ﴿and they mock﴾, i.e., they mock that statement of yours about the Resurrection and its possibility. As for His words, ﴿And when they are reminded﴾, i.e., by the verses, so that they might remember and believe and affirm the Oneness of Allah, ﴿they do not remember﴾, because of the hardness of their hearts and the darkness of their sins through shirk and disobedience. As for His words, ﴿And when they see a sign, they ridicule it﴾, i.e., they mock and deride it, ﴿and they say: "This is nothing but clear magic"﴾, i.e., what Muhammad ﷺ has brought in word and deed is nothing but manifest magic, i.e., clear and evident. In this they are certainly lying, distinguishing between magic, which is false imagination, and the truth established by reason and revelation, from the fine points of the Sharia and the fundamentals of religion, such as faith in Allah and the Last Day. As for His words, ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?"﴾, this is the saying of the deniers among the polytheists, who say it in amazement and as those who consider the Resurrection far-fetched. Allah the Exalted says in reply: Say, O Our Messenger, to them: ﴿Yes﴾, you will be resurrected alive, ﴿and you will be abased﴾, i.e., humiliated and degraded. The matter of your return requires no more than that Israfil blows into the Trumpet, and then you will be alive, coming out of your graves. ﴿It will be but a single shout﴾, i.e., a cry, ﴿and behold, they will be standing and looking﴾, and they will say, upon rising from their graves: ﴿"Woe to us!"﴾, i.e., O our destruction, come, this is your time to appear. That is, they call down destruction upon themselves because of the severity of what they witness of the terror of the Resurrection, like the saying of one of them: "Would that it had been the end [of me]!"

Their saying, "This is the Day of Judgment," is an acknowledgment by them of the Resurrection and the Recompense, but at a time when acknowledgment will not benefit them. That is, this is the Day of Reckoning and Recompense. Then it will be said to them: ﴿This is the Day of Decision﴾, on which Allah the Exalted will decide between His servants concerning what they used to differ about, judging among them with justice. As for His words, ﴿which you used to deny﴾, it is a rebuke to them, i.e., this is the Day of Resurrection that you used to deny, saying in disbelief: "When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected? Or our forefathers too?"

1- Explanation of the origin of human creation, which is sticky clay, i.e., clay that clings to the hand.

2- Explanation of two opposing positions: the Messenger is amazed at the disbelief and denial of the polytheists, while the polytheists mock his call to them to faith and to not denying Allah and meeting Him.

3- Establishment of the Resurrection and explanation of how it will occur.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 22–30:

Explanation of the words:

"Gather those who did wrong": that is, themselves, through shirk (association of partners with God) and sins.

"And their spouses": that is, their companions from the devils (shayatin).

"Besides God": that is, apart from God, [such as] idols and images.

"Then guide them": that is, direct them and drive them.

"To the path of Hellfire": that is, to the road of the Fire.

"And stop them, for they are to be questioned": that is, detain them at the Sirat (the Bridge/Path), for they are to be questioned about all their words and deeds.

"What is [the matter] with you that you do not help one another?": that is, why is it that none of you helps another, as you used to in the world, as a rebuke to them.

"Indeed, you used to come to us from the right": that is, from the right side of one of us, making falsehood appear attractive to him and making evil seem good to him, so that you command him to shirk and forbid him from monotheism (tawhid).

"They will say, 'Rather, you were not believers'": that is, their companions from the jinn will answer them in refutation, "Rather, you were not believers to begin with."

"And we had no authority over you": that is, no proof, nor any power to compel you to shirk, evil and falsehood.

"Rather, you were a transgressing people": that is, rather, you were tyrants and wrongdoers who worshipped other than God and compelled people to do so.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains the scene of the Standing-place of the Resurrection, where, after their acknowledgment that this is the Day of Judgment, and God's response to them with His saying, ﴿This is the Day of Decision which you used to deny﴾ [al-Saffat: 21], the Mighty, Majestic One says, ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, meaning: gather those who did wrong through shirk and sins. His saying, ﴿and their spouses﴾, means their companions from the jinn, ﴿and what they used to worship besides God﴾, [such as] the idols and images. And the saying of the Exalted, ﴿Then guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾, the Mighty and Majestic God says: then guide them, that is, direct them to the road of the Fire.

And He says, ﴿and stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾, then they are questioned, ﴿What is [the matter] with you that you do not help one another?﴾, meaning: why does none of you help another as you did in the world? How could they help one another in such a terrifying standing? Rather, they are today submitting, that is, submissive and humbled. And the saying of the Exalted, ﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning each other﴾, means: the followers turn to their leaders, questioning one another, that is, blaming each other, each casting responsibility onto the other. So the followers from mankind say to their companions from the jinn what God has reported about them: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right﴾, that is, and from the left, meaning: you used to whisper to us, making shirk and evil seem good to us, rather commanding us to it and urging us upon it. Their companions answered them with what God has reported in His saying, ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers."﴾, meaning: you were not believers, so we disbelieved you; nor were you righteous, so we corrupted you; nor were you monotheists, so we led you to shirk. This is the first point. Second, ﴿And we had no authority over you﴾, that is, no compelling proofs by which we convinced you, nor any power by which we forced you, so you followed us. Rather, you yourselves were a transgressing people, that is, wrongdoers who exceeded the limit in extravagance, injustice and evil.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A depiction of one of the scenes of the Standing-place of the Resurrection.

2- Clarification that those alike in disbelief, in wickedness, or in deviance are gathered together with one another.

3- The uselessness of the worshippers disavowing the worshipped, and the followers' argument against their leaders.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verse 31–37:

Explanation of the words:

﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us﴾: i.e., the punishment became due upon us.

﴿Indeed, we are to taste [it]﴾: i.e., we and you will taste the punishment.

﴿So we led you astray; indeed, we were ourselves astray﴾: i.e., we misguided you, for we were ourselves misguided.

﴿Indeed, they, that Day, will be sharers in the punishment﴾: i.e., on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿in the punishment, sharing [it together]﴾: because they had been sharers in the deviation.

﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals﴾: just as We punished these followers and leaders, We punish the followers and leaders in every misguidance, disbelief and corruption.

﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them: "There is no deity except Allah," would be arrogant﴾: i.e., those polytheists, the worshippers of idols, when the Messenger said to them:

﴿"There is no deity except Allah," they were arrogant﴾: i.e., say "There is no deity except Allah" and worship none but Allah, they were arrogant and would not say it or affirm His oneness.

﴿"Are we to leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾: they meant Muhammad ﷺ.

﴿Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers﴾: i.e., rather, he has brought "There is no deity except Allah," which is the truth that all the messengers brought, and he confirmed them in what they brought before him, which is monotheism (tawhid).

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with what Allah mentioned of the questions of the wrongdoers and what the followers said to the leaders and what the leaders said to the followers. His saying, ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us; indeed, we are to taste [it]﴾, is the saying of the leaders to their followers: they said to them, because of our deviation and misguidance the punishment became due upon us, and upon you, that we will taste it without doubt. They also said to them, acknowledging their misguiding of them: ﴿So we led you astray; indeed, we were ourselves astray﴾. This is the saying of the jinn to mankind. Allah said: ﴿Indeed, they, that Day, will be sharers in the punishment﴾, because they shared in polytheism, evil and corruption. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals﴾ refers to the other categories, such as adulterers, usurers and shedders of blood; We punish each category together with its kind. This refers back to His saying: "Gather those who did wrong and their spouses," i.e., their companions and their likes.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them: "There is no deity except Allah," were arrogant﴾ informs us that the polytheists of Quraysh, in the world, when the Messenger of Allah or one of the believers said to them, "Say: There is no deity except Allah," were arrogant and turned away, and would not say it. Rather they said: ﴿"Are we to leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾, meaning the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. They described the Qur'an as poetry, and Muhammad ﷺ, who recited and read it, as a poet, and what he called them to of belief in the resurrection and recompense as madness; in their view the Messenger was mad. Allah replied to them with His saying: ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth﴾, i.e., our Messenger is not a poet nor mad, but has brought the truth, which you denied and rejected out of blind following and obstinacy, so you said what you said. Rather, he has brought the truth, which is "There is no deity except Allah," ﴿and confirmed the messengers﴾ who came before him with the word "There is no deity except Allah," calling to it, and who lived and died upon it.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Clarification of the destruction of the one who goes astray and of the one who misleads him, and of the deviant and the one who leads him astray.

2- Clarification of the baseless accusations the polytheists directed at the Messenger of Allah, and Allah's refutation of them.

3- Exalting the status of "There is no deity except Allah," and that it is the call of all the messengers who preceded the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

4- Affirmation of monotheism, the resurrection, recompense and the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verse 38–49:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And you are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾ That is: none is recompensed except for the recompense of what you used to do of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and sins.

﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah.﴾ That is: but the sincere servants of Allah, meaning those who worship Allah alone, for they are recompensed with more than their deeds, since a good deed is rewarded tenfold and more.

﴿For them is a known provision.﴾ That is: in Paradise, morning and evening.

﴿Fruits.﴾ That is: their food and drink there is for enjoyment, just as one enjoys fruits, and it is not for sustaining their bodies alive as in this world.

﴿And they will be honoured.﴾ That is: no humiliation will touch them there, but it will be said to them, "Enjoy it with health (hani'an)," in contrast to the people of the Fire, to whom it will be said, "Taste the punishment of the Fire for what you used to do."

﴿From a flowing spring.﴾ That is: flowing upon the surface of the earth like flowing springs of water.

﴿Delicious to the drinkers.﴾ That is: the wine is described as being delicious to those who drink it.

﴿No headache is in it.⁠﴾ That is: nothing that would seize their minds and bodies and destroy them.

﴿Nor will they be intoxicated by it.﴾ That is: they will not become drunk because of it, as is the case with the wine of this world.

﴿With women restraining their gazes.﴾ That is: they do not look at anyone other than their husbands, because of their beauty and loveliness in their eyes.

﴿With wide, beautiful eyes.﴾ That is: having large eyes; the singular is ʿaynāʾ.

﴿As if they were protected eggs.﴾ That is: as if they were hidden eggs, concealed, not reached by dust or anything else.

Explanation of the meanings of the verses:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, you will taste the painful punishment, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.﴾ This is said to the people of the Fire, who will be held in place and will question one another, and among what will be said to them at that time is this statement, so they will be informed that they will taste the painful, agonising punishment, and that they are recompensed only in accordance with what they used to do. They will not be wronged in the recompense; rather it is a just recompense, a bad deed repaid with its like. Here Allah the Exalted excepted the recompense of His believing servants whom He chose for His worship, so they worshipped Him and affirmed His oneness, for they are recompensed with more than their deeds, as a bounty from Him and a kindness to them. A good deed is rewarded tenfold and more, up to seven hundred and beyond. So He said: ﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah.﴾ Then Allah the Exalted explained some of their recompense, saying: ﴿Those – for them is a known provision﴾, that is, they will eat it morning and evening. His saying "fruits" indicates that they do not eat or drink to preserve their bodies from death and perishing; rather they eat what they eat and drink what they drink for enjoyment of it, not to ward off the torment of hunger as in this world. ﴿And they will be honoured﴾, that is, in Paradise, where no humiliation will ever touch them. His saying "in the Gardens of Bliss" attributes the Garden to bliss, emphasising its description as blissful, to the extent that the Garden is made the Garden of Bliss, thus making a garden for bliss, which is itself bliss. He informed that they will be reclining there on couches facing one another, looking at one another, while in a state of enjoyment. He also informed about them that, while seated facing one another, they will be served by special servants from among the angels. So He said: ﴿They will be circulated among with a cup from a flowing spring﴾, that is, of wine flowing with rivers as if they were springs of water. He described the wine as white, as a great delight for those who drink it, and as having no headache in it, which is what would seize their bodies, such as migraine and stomach pain. So He said: ﴿No headache is in it, nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, that is, they will not become intoxicated so as to have their minds taken away.

His saying ﴿And with them will be women restraining their gazes﴾ means that they will have wives, and "restraining their gazes" means that they confine their looks to their husbands and do not look at others, because of their beauty and loveliness; each one of them looks only at her husband. His saying ﴿with wide, beautiful eyes﴾ means having large eyes. ﴿As if they were protected eggs﴾: this is a description of the women of Paradise, that their bodies are white, with a whiteness like that of ostrich eggs, which is white tinged with yellow, and this is among the finest kinds of beauty in women. The meaning of ﴿protected﴾ is hidden, untouched by dust or any harm.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- A demonstration of the justice of the Truth, blessed and exalted, in that He repays a bad deed with its like, and does not hold anyone accountable for other than what they earned in the worldly life.

2- A demonstration of Allah the Exalted's bounty, in that He repays believers' good deeds tenfold, up to more than seven hundred.

3- Affirmation of the Resurrection and an explanation of some of what takes place in it of speech and action.

4- A description of the bliss of the people of Paradise in food, drink, sitting and enjoyment.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verse 50–61:

Explanation of the words:

﴿فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾ (fa-aqbala ba'duhum 'ala ba'd): i.e., the people of Paradise turned to one another.

﴿يَتَسَاءَلُونَ﴾ (yatasa'alun): i.e., about what had passed them by in the world and what had happened to them there.

﴿إِنِّي كَانَ لِي قَرِينٌ﴾ (inni kana li qarin): i.e., I had a companion who denied the Last Resurrection.

﴿يَقُولُ أَئِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصَدِّقِينَ﴾ (yaqulu a'innaka laminal-musaddiqin): i.e., he would say, as a rebuke and reproach to me, "Are you truly among those who affirm [the resurrection and the recompense]?"

﴿أَءِنَّا لَمَدِينُونَ﴾ (a'inna lamadinun): i.e., "Shall we indeed be called to account and recompensed for our deeds in the world?" — said in denial and rejection.

﴿هَلْ أَنتُم مُّطَّلِعُونَ﴾ (hal antum muttali'un): i.e., "Would you like to look down with me [into the Fire] so that we may see his condition and the punishment he is in?"

﴿فَاطَّلَعَ فَرَآهُ فِي سَوَاءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾ (fattala'a fara'ahu fi sawa'il-jahim): i.e., in the midst of the Fire.

﴿تَٱللَّهِ إِن كِدتَّ لَتُرْدِينِ﴾ (tallahi in kidta latirdin): i.e., he said this gloating over him; and "tardin" means "you would destroy me."

﴿وَلَوْلَا نِعْمَةُ رَبِّي لَكُنتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ﴾ (wa lawla ni'matu rabbi lakuntu minal-muhdarin): i.e., "had it not been for my Lord's favor, I would have been among those brought forth [into Hell]."

﴿أَفَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَيِّتِينَ﴾ (afama nahnu bimayyitin): i.e., "Are we then not to die, [but to remain forever]? The interrogative here is for affirmation, meaning: yes."

﴿إِلَّا مَوْتَتَنَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ﴾ (illa mawtatana al-ula): i.e., the first death which we died in the world.

﴿لِمِثْلِ هَٰذَا فَلْيَعْمَلِ ٱلْعَامِلُونَ﴾ (limithli hadha falya'mali al-'amilun): i.e., for the like of this bliss, the eternal abiding in Paradise and its delights, let the workers work; and that is by abundance of righteous deeds and avoidance of evil deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to explain the bliss of the people of Paradise. Having sat on couches facing one another, conversing and recalling what had happened to them in the life of this world, one of them said: I once had a companion in the world, who would say to me, mockingly and in denial of the Last Resurrection: ﴿Are you truly among those who affirm it?﴾ — that is, the resurrection and recompense for deeds in the world. He also said, in disbelief and denial: ﴿When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we indeed be called to account and recompensed?﴾ — that is, held accountable and repaid. Then that speaker said to some of those present, ﴿Would you look down with me?﴾ — that is, [to look] at the people of the Fire with me, so that we may see my companion there and ask him about his state. It seems they refused and declined to look. He, however, looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire. He then said to him what God reported of him in His words: ﴿By God, you almost ruined me!﴾ — that is, "by Allah" — ﴿you nearly destroyed me,﴾ because you used to deny me faith in the resurrection, mock me, and gloat over me for my faith and righteous deeds, whose reward I hoped for, and which is now fully realized. He also said: ﴿Had it not been for the favor of my Lord upon me in protection and preservation, I would have been among those brought forth [into Hell] along with you now.﴾ Then he said to him: ﴿Are we then not to die, except our first death?﴾ The interrogative is affirmative: he is asserting it, so that he might say, "Yes, we are abiding forever — we in Paradise and you in the Fire." Then he said that this — that is, abiding forever in the abode of bliss — ﴿is indeed the supreme triumph,﴾ since it is deliverance from the Fire, the greatest thing to be feared and dreaded, and entry into Paradise, the abode of peace and enduring delight. God says: ﴿For the like of this, let the workers work,﴾ — that is, this great triumph of deliverance from the Fire and eternal abiding in the abode of the righteous — ﴿so let the workers work,﴾ that is, let them persevere in their deeds and make them sincerely for God, Lord of the worlds.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Demonstration of God's greatness in enabling the believer to speak with one who is in the midst of Hell, to see his image, to address him, and to understand one another; and the television broadcast today has made this reality easier to grasp.

2- Warning against evil companions, such as the atheist youth and others.

3- Illustration of how the deniers used to mock the believers and regard them as intellectually deficient.

4- There is no death in the Hereafter, only eternal life in bliss or in Hell.

5- Encouragement to abundant righteous deeds and distance from corrupt deeds.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 62–74:

Explanation of the words:

"Is that better as an entertainment (nuzul)?": That is, what has been mentioned for the people of Paradise is better as a nuzul, which is what is prepared for a guest or any other arrival, such as hospitality.

"Or the tree of Zaqqum?": Prepared for the people of the Fire. It is one of the most foul trees in taste and bitterness.

"Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers": That is, a test and an examination for them in this world, and a punishment for them in the Hereafter.

"It springs from the root of Hell": That is, from the bottom of Hell, and its branches are in its levels.

"Its fruit-stalks are like the heads of devils": That is, what first emerges from its fruit is like ugly-looking serpents.

"Then indeed they will have upon it a mixture of boiling water": That is, after eating it they will be given boiling water to drink, and that mixture (shawb) is a blending.

"Indeed they found their fathers astray": That is, they found their fathers already going astray.

"So they are hastening in their footsteps": That is, they hurry, rushing to follow them without thought or deliberation.

"And We had already sent among them warners": That is, messengers warning them of the punishment.

"Then see how was the end of those who were warned": It was a painful punishment because of their persistence in disbelief.

"Except the chosen servants of Allah": They were saved from the punishment and were not destroyed.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah mentioned what He had prepared for those who believe in Him and obey Him and His Messenger, of lasting bliss in the Paradise, the abode of the righteous, He said: "Is that mentioned bliss in Paradise better as a nuzul?" The nuzul is what is prepared as provision for a guest or any other arrival. "Or the tree of Zaqqum?" That is, its fruit, which is a loathsome, bitter, ugly-looking fruit. Then Allah informed that He made it a trial for the wrongdoers, among the disbelievers of Quraysh, when they heard of it and said: how can a tree grow in the Fire when the Fire burns trees? So they denied it, and that became a trial for them. Then He described it, saying: "Indeed, it is a tree that springs from the root of Hell", that is, from its bottom, and its branches extend through the levels of the Fire. His words "its fruit-stalks" refer to what emerges from its fruit, in its ugly appearance: "like the heads of devils", because the Arabs use the devil as an example of ugliness, just as there are serpents they call "devils" that are ugly in appearance. His words "Indeed they will eat from it" mean that the wrongdoing polytheists will eat from the tree of Zaqqum because of their extreme hunger, "and fill their bellies with it", that is, their bellies. "Then indeed they will have upon it a mixture of boiling water": when they eat, they become thirsty and are given boiling water to drink; that mixture of boiling water is the shawb, meaning a blending and mixing, as one says "the milk was mixed (shaba) with water", meaning he mixed it in. His words "Then indeed their return is to Hell": that is, their return to the Hell after they have eaten and drunk in gatherings specifically for eating and drinking, they are sent back to the Fire of Hell.

His words "Indeed they found their fathers astray": that is, they found their fathers straying from the path of guidance and righteousness. "So they are hastening in their footsteps": that is, they run quickly behind them, following them in polytheism, disbelief and misguidance. His words "And most of the former peoples had already gone astray before them": that is, these are not the first to go astray. "And We had already sent among them": among those earlier nations who went astray, "warners", that is, messengers warning them, but they did not believe, so We destroyed them. "Then see how was the end of those who were warned": it was destruction and ruin for the disbelievers. His words "Except the chosen servants of Allah" are an exception from Him for His believing, righteous servants, who are those He chose for His worship through His remembrance and gratitude, so they believed and obeyed; He saved them and destroyed their disbelieving, denying enemies. In the verses there is a threat and warning to the disbelievers of Quraysh that admits of no greater.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Demonstration of the best methods of calling to Islam, which are warning and encouragement.

2- Affirmation of resurrection and recompense through presenting the events that take place on the Day of Resurrection.

3- Condemnation of blindly following fathers, forefathers and the people of one's land in misguidance.

4- Allah's destruction of wrongdoers and His rescue of believers, both when sins are punished in this world and in the Hereafter.

"Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers": That is, a test and an examination for them in this world, and a punishment for them in the Hereafter.

"It springs from the root of Hell": That is, from the bottom of Hell, and its branches are in its levels.

"Its fruit-stalks are like the heads of devils": That is, what first emerges from its fruit is like ugly-looking serpents.

**Explanation of Words:**

﴿And Nuh certainly called upon Us﴾: that is, he said, "I am overpowered, so help me," (from Surah al-Qamar).

﴿So how excellent were the Responders﴾: that is, to him, when We saved him and destroyed the disbelievers among his people.

﴿From the great distress﴾: that is, the punishment of drowning by the flood.

﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾: since most people were descended from his sons Sam, Ham and Yafith.

﴿And We left for him a good mention among later generations﴾: that is, We kept for him a good praise among all nations and peoples.

﴿Peace be upon Nuh among the worlds﴾: that is, peace from Us upon Nuh among the worlds, that is, among all people.

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾: that is, just as We rewarded Nuh with a good mention and peace among the worlds, We reward the doers of good.

﴿Then We drowned the others﴾: that is, the polytheist disbelievers of his people, after We saved the believers in the Ark.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

Following His mention of the destruction of those who were warned and the salvation of His sincere believing servants, Allah related a historical account of this, namely Nuh and his people. Nuh warned his people, and when the punishment came, Allah saved His sincere servants and destroyed the deniers who had been warned. Allah said, in relating this concise story, ﴿And Nuh certainly called upon Us﴾, that is, he called on Us for help against his people, ﴿He said, "My Lord, help me, for they have denied me"﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 26, 39], and he said, ﴿"I am overpowered, so help me"﴾ [Al-Qamar: 10]. ﴿So how excellent were the Responders﴾, We were, for him. ﴿And We saved him and his family﴾, except for his wife and his son Kan'an, ﴿from the great distress﴾, which is the punishment of drowning.

His saying, ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾, until the Day of Resurrection, was a reward for him for his patience in his call, his sincerity and his truthfulness in it, since all people today are descended from his three sons: Sam, who is the father of the Arabs, the Romans and the Persians; Ham, who is the father of the Sudanese; and Yafith, who is the father of the Turks and the Khazars, who are the Tatars with narrow eyes, which is why they were called Khazar, from *khazar al-ayn*, meaning narrowness and smallness of the eyes; and Ya'juj and Ma'juj. His saying, ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾, that is, among the generations of mankind that came after him, is the good mention and the fragrant praise, expressed by His saying, ﴿Peace be upon Nuh among the worlds﴾. His saying, ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾, means: just as We rewarded Nuh for his faith, patience, piety, truthfulness, sincere counsel and devotion, We reward the doers of good in their faith and piety. This is good news for the believers. His saying, ﴿Indeed he was among Our believing servants﴾, is praise of him and a statement of the cause of honouring and favouring him, and an invitation to faith through encouragement toward it. His saying, ﴿Then We drowned the others﴾, means: We drowned them by the flood because of their disbelief, their polytheism and their denial, after We had saved the believers.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The demonstration of Allah's honouring of His friends and His humiliating of His enemies.
2. The answering of the supplication of the righteous, especially when they are wronged.
3. The virtue of doing good and the good end of its people.
4. The virtue of faith and the dignity of its people with Allah in this world and the Hereafter.
5. Saying "Peace be upon Nuh among the worlds" when a believer says it in the evening or the morning, Allah protects him from the sting of a scorpion. And more authentic than it is the saying: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created," because of the soundness of the hadith (a report from the Prophet ﷺ) concerning that.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 83–98:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And indeed, among his followers was Ibrahim﴾: that is, among the adherents of Nuh, upon his creed (millah) and method (minhaj), was Ibrahim al-Khalil (the Friend of God), peace be upon them both.

﴿When he came to his Lord with a sound heart﴾: that is, he came to his Lord with a heart sound of shirk (association of partners with God), of doubt, and of turning toward anyone other than the Lord, glorified and exalted is He.

﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?"﴾: that is, when he said to his father and his polytheist people, "What is the thing you worship?"

﴿Is it a falsehood, gods other than God, that you desire?﴾: that is, do you desire, as a lie that is the worst of lies, gods other than God?

﴿What then is your assumption about the Lord of the worlds?﴾: that is, what is it? Do you think He will not be angry with you nor punish you, so that you worship other than Him, while He is your Lord and the Lord of the worlds?

﴿Then he glanced at the stars﴾: that is, to deceive them, since they used to deify the stars.

﴿And said, "Indeed, I am sick"﴾: that is, ill, one afflicted with sickness, which is disease and ailment.

﴿So they turned away from him, retreating﴾: that is, they returned to what they were engaged in and left him, accepting his excuse.

﴿Then he went secretly to their gods﴾: that is, he turned to them covertly.

﴿And struck them with the right hand﴾: that is, with the strength of his right hand, he broke them with an axe and smashed them.

﴿Then they came hastening toward him﴾: that is, they walked with strength and speed.

﴿What you carve﴾: of stones, wood and metals such as gold and silver.

﴿And what you make﴾: that is, and God created what you worship of idols and stars.

﴿They said, "Build for him a structure"﴾: fill it with firewood, set the fire alight, and when it blazes, throw him into it.

﴿So We made them the lowest﴾: that is, the vanquished and defeated, frustrated in their scheme, when God saved Ibrahim.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted mentioned the story of Nuh, affirming thereby the support of His allies and the abandonment of His enemies, He mentioned another story, the story of Ibrahim, which is the greatest admonition for the disbelievers of Quraysh, because they trace their lineage to Ibrahim and claim to follow his creed and the creed of his son Isma'il. Therefore He extended the account of it. He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, among his followers was Ibrahim﴾, that is, among the adherents of Nuh who follow his creed and method was Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful. ﴿When he came to his Lord with a sound heart﴾, that is, he came to his Lord with a heart sound of shirk, of doubt, and of turning toward anyone other than the Lord, exalted is He, at the time he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?", denouncing to them their worship of idols. Had there been in his heart the slightest inclination toward other than God, out of desire or fear, he would not have been able to say what he said; rather, at that moment his heart was sound, with no regard for anyone other than God, exalted is He. His saying ﴿Is it a falsehood, gods other than God, that you desire?﴾ means: is it a lie, the worst of lies, that you desire gods other than God, since you have made them, by your lying tongues, gods, while they are only stones and idols. His saying ﴿What then is your assumption about the Lord of the worlds?﴾, when you have worshipped falsehood instead of Him, since your gods are nothing but pure falsehood. Do you think that God will not be angry with you nor punish you?

His saying ﴿Then he glanced at the stars and said, "Indeed, I am sick"﴾: here there is an omitted statement indicated by the context, namely that the people of the town had resolved to go out to a festival of theirs which they would spend outside the town. They invited him to go out with them, and he excused himself by saying, "Indeed, I am sick," that is, one afflicted with sickness, after he had looked at the stars, giving them the impression that he had seen what indicated he would be stricken with sickness, namely the plague. The people were astrologers who looked at the stars and claimed that through them they knew the good and evil that descend to the earth by means of the planets. Thus he deceived them, and they left him out of fear of the contagion of the plague, or they left him accepting his excuse. This is what is indicated by the Exalted's saying ﴿Then he glanced at the stars and said, "Indeed, I am sick"﴾. ﴿So they turned away from him﴾, that is, because of that, and returned to their affairs and what they were resolved upon of going out to the festival outside the town; this is the meaning of ﴿they turned away from him, retreating﴾. Then the place where the gods were was left free of guards, worshippers and visitors to the gods in their private hall, so he carried out what he had sworn to do in a dispute that had occurred between him and some of them, when he said: ﴿And by God, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone﴾ [al-Anbiya': 57], and he began the task. He said to the gods, with varieties of food before them, such foods as sweets and others which the polytheists leave to be blessed by the gods and then eat, hoping for their blessing: ﴿Will you not eat?﴾, offering them the food mockingly. They did not answer him or eat, so he said to them: ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not speak?﴾ Then he fell upon them, striking them with an axe in his right hand, and broke them into pieces, scattered fragments. When they returned from their festival in the evening and came to the hall of the gods to take the food, they found the gods broken. ﴿Then they came hastening toward him﴾, that is, quickly, having asked their men to bring him immediately; they brought him and began to interrogate him. He said in his defense: ﴿Do you worship what you carve?﴾, that is, with your hands, idols some of which are of stone, some of wood, and some of silver and of gold as well, ﴿while God created you and what you make﴾ of every deed of yours. Why then do you not worship Him, and worship idols that neither benefit nor harm? When he overcame them in argument and they were defeated before him, they issued their order to burn him with fire. They said: ﴿Build for him a structure﴾, that is, a great furnace, fill it with firewood, set the fire alight until it blazes, then throw him into its blaze. This is the meaning of the Exalted's saying: ﴿They said, "Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire."﴾ His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and they intended a scheme﴾, that is, against Ibrahim, ﴿a scheme﴾, that is, evil, by their resolve to burn him and their carrying out of what they had resolved. ﴿So We made them the lowest﴾, that is, the defeated and vanquished, when the Exalted said to the fire: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe for Ibrahim﴾ [al-Anbiya': 69]. It became so, and Ibrahim came out of it, and only his bonds that were on his hands and feet were burned. God frustrated the efforts of the polytheists and humiliated and disgraced them before Ibrahim, and this is the meaning of the Exalted's saying ﴿So We made them the most losers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 70]. God the Exalted combined for them loss in everything they had hoped for from their deeds, and that loss never left them.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The root of religion is one: Islam is the religion of God with which Adam and those after him up to Muhammad (ﷺ) worshipped.

2- The perfection of Ibrahim in the soundness of his heart from turning toward anyone other than God, to the extent that Jibril appeared to him while he was on his way to the furnace his people had prepared for him, and said: [Do you have any need, O Ibrahim? He said: As for you, no.]

3- Among the most abominable lies is the claim that other than God is worshipped alongside God, seeking blessing through it or seeking its intercession.

4- The obligation to change wrongdoing when one is able to do so.

5- Clarification of Ibrahim's trial, and that he was thrown into the fire and was patient; therefore his Lord honored him with what will be explained later in the context.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 99–113:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Inni dhahibun ila rabbi sayahdin﴾: that is, "I am emigrating to my Lord; He will guide me" to a place where I may worship Him, and where I will not be prevented from worshipping Him.

﴿Rabbi hab li min as-salihin﴾: that is, "grant me a child from among the righteous."

﴿Bi-ghulamin halim﴾: that is, a child who will be possessed of forbearance and much patience.

﴿Falamma balagha ma'ahu as-sa'y﴾: that is, when he reached the age at which he was able to work, about seven years or more.

﴿Fanzur madha tara﴾: that is, "what is your opinion, in matters of right judgement?"

﴿Min as-sabirin﴾: that is, "patient in face of the slaughter I have been commanded to carry out."

﴿Falamma aslama﴾: that is, the son and the father both submitted to the command of God and yielded to Him.

﴿Wa tallahu lil-jabin﴾: that is, he threw him down upon his forehead, by placing his forehead on the ground. Every human being has two temples, right and left, and the forehead lies between them.

﴿Qad saddaqta ar-ru'ya﴾: that is, for what you resolved upon and carried out: going forth with the son to Mina, throwing him down on the ground, and passing the knife over his throat.

﴿Inna hadha lahuwa al-bala' al-mubin﴾: that is, the command to slaughter was a great trial.

﴿Wa fadaynahu bi-dhibhin 'azim﴾: that is, a large ram.

﴿Wa taraknа 'alayhi fi al-akhirin﴾: that is, We left for him a good praise and a good remembrance among the people who came after him.

﴿Wa barakna 'alayhi wa 'ala Ishaq﴾: that is, We blessed him by multiplying his offspring and the offspring of Isaac, so that most of the prophets are from their descendants.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the story of Abraham, the Friend (of God). After he was thrown into the fire and came out safe by the praise of God, he decided to emigrate and leave the land, and said, ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me﴾, meaning: I am going to where my Lord has permitted me to emigrate, where I can worship Him. So he went to the land of Syria and first settled in Harran in Syria. His words "He will guide me" mean that He will keep me firm through His continuous guidance to me. He prayed to his Lord, saying, ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous﴾, meaning: provide me with righteous children. God answered him: he travelled to the land of Jerusalem with his wife Sarah and reached Egypt. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 99–113:

The noble context continues with the story of Abraham, the Friend (of God). After he was thrown into the fire and came out safe by the praise of God, he decided to emigrate and leave the land, and said, ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me﴾, meaning: I am going to where my Lord has permitted me to emigrate, where I can worship Him. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 114–122:

Explanation of the words:

"And We certainly bestowed favour upon Musa and Harun": that is, with prophethood and messengership.

"And We delivered them and their people": that is, the Children of Israel.

"From the great distress": that is, Pharaoh's enslavement of them and his persecution of them.

"And We helped them": against Pharaoh and his soldiers.

"The clear Book": that is, the Torah, clear in its rulings and laws.

"And We guided them to the straight path": that is, Islam, submission to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

"And We left for them among later generations": that is, We kept for them a good remembrance among later generations.

"Peace upon Musa and Harun": that is, peace from Us upon Musa and Harun.

"Indeed, that is how We reward the doers of good": that is, just as We rewarded them, We reward the good-doers among Our believing servants.

"Indeed, they were among Our believing servants": that is, We rewarded them with what We rewarded them with because of their faith.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to mention Allah's bounty and grace upon whomever He wills of His servants. After mentioning His favour upon Ibrahim and his son Ishaq, He mentions from their descendants the good-doers Musa and Harun, saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly bestowed favour upon Musa and Harun﴾, that is, with prophethood and messengership, ﴿and We delivered them and their people﴾, that is, the Children of Israel, ﴿from the great distress﴾, which was the enslavement imposed on them by Pharaoh and the Copts and their persecution for a long time, ﴿and We helped them﴾, that is, against Pharaoh and his chiefs, ﴿so they were the victors﴾. ﴿And We gave them﴾, that is, We bestowed upon them, ﴿the clear Book﴾, which is the Torah, clear in its rulings and evident in its laws, with no obscurity or ambiguity in it. ﴿And We guided them to the straight path﴾, which is the correct religion, which is Islam, the religion of Allah with which He sent all His messengers. ﴿And We left for them among later generations﴾, that is, We kept for them a good remembrance and a fragrant praise among those who came after them. ﴿Peace upon Musa and Harun﴾. ﴿Indeed, that is how We reward the doers of good﴾, that is, just as We rewarded them for their good deeds, We reward the good-doers. ﴿Indeed, they were among Our believing servants﴾: this explains the cause of the bounty and favour He bestowed upon them, which is faith, which necessitates submission (Islam) and excellence (ihsan).

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of Allah's honouring of His two messengers, Musa and Harun, peace be upon them.

2- Explanation of Allah's favour upon the Children of Israel by delivering them from the people of Pharaoh and granting them victory over them.

3- Explanation that Islam is the religion of all the prophets, and is not specific to the Muslim nation.

4- Explanation of the excellence of ihsan and faith.

Explanation of the terms:

And indeed Ilyas (Elias) was among the messengers: Ilyas is one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, from the lineage of Harun (Aaron), whom God sent to the people of the city of Ba'albak in al-Sham (Greater Syria).

Do you call upon Ba'l: that is, an idol called Ba'l.

And leave the best of creators: that is, and you abandon the worship of God, the best of creators.

Indeed they will be brought forward (to the Fire): that is, into the Fire.

Except the sincere servants of God: that is, they were saved from the Fire.

And We left for him among the later generations: that is, We preserved for him a good remembrance among the later generations.

Peace be upon the family of Yasin: that is, peace from Us upon Ilyas.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to mention God's favour upon some of His prophets and messengers. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed Ilyas was among the messengers﴾. He is from the lineage of Harun, peace be upon him, one of the prophets of the Children of Israel. God informs that he was among the messengers, meaning: remember when he said to his people, who were the people of the city of Ba'albak and its surroundings: ﴿Will you not fear (God)?﴾, that is, God, by worshipping Him and abandoning the worship of other than Him. This is evidence that he was a messenger. His saying, peace be upon him, ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l?﴾ is a denunciation from him of them for worshipping a great idol of theirs which they call Ba'l; that is, how can you worship an idol by calling upon it, devoting yourselves to it, slaughtering for it and vowing to it, and abandon the worship of God, the best of creators, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old? He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But they denied him﴾, that is, regarding his saying that there is no god but God, ﴿and they will surely be brought forward (to the Fire)﴾ [At-Tawbah: 125]; so they will be brought into Hell and are among those brought forward therein. His, exalted is He, saying ﴿except the sincere servants of God﴾ means the monotheists, for they are not in the Fire but are in Paradise. His, exalted is He, saying ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ means: We preserved for him a good remembrance among the people who came after him. His saying ﴿Peace﴾, that is, from Us, ﴿be upon the family of Yasin﴾. ﴿Indeed, thus﴾, that is, just as We rewarded Ilyas for his good conduct in obeying Us, ﴿We reward the good-doers﴾. His saying ﴿Indeed he was among Our believing servants﴾ means: he deserved Our honouring and good reward because he was among Our believing servants.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of monotheism and denunciation of polytheism.

2- The destruction of the polytheists and the salvation of the monotheists on the Day of Resurrection.

3- The virtue of excellence (ihsan) and the recompense of its people with good reward.

4- The virtue of faith, and that it is the cause of every good and perfection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 133–138:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa inna Lutan lamina al-mursalin* (And indeed Lot was among the messengers): That is, Lot, who was the son of Haran, the brother of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), was also among the body of messengers.

*Idh najjaynahu wa ahlahu ajma'in* (When We saved him and his family, all of them): That is, remember, O Messenger, among those whom We favoured with prophethood and messengership, Lot, when We saved him and his family, all of them, from the punishment of the evil rain.

*Illa 'ajuzan fi al-ghabirin* (Except an old woman among those who remained behind): That is, except his wife, the disbelieving one, who was destroyed among those who remained (al-ghabirin), meaning those left behind in the punishment.

*Thumma dammarna al-akharin* (Then We destroyed the others): That is, We destroyed the others, apart from Lot and the believers with him.

*Wa innakum latamurrna 'alayhim* (And indeed you pass by them): That is, on your journeys to Palestine, Gaza and Egypt, by night and by day.

*Afala ta'qilun* (Will you not then reason?): That is, O people of Makkah, consider what befell them, so that you may take warning, be admonished, and believe and affirm the Oneness of God.

Explanation of the verses:

The discourse continues to mention God's favour upon those whom He chose from among His servants. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And indeed Lot﴾, who was the son of Haran, the brother of Abraham, peace be upon them both, ﴿was among the messengers﴾, that is, among the body of Our messengers. ﴿When We saved him﴾, that is, remember Our favour upon him when We saved him from the punishment, ﴿and his family, all of them﴾. ﴿Except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾, and she was his wife, for she was with the disbelievers, so she remained with them and was destroyed with their destruction. His saying, exalted be He, ﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾, that is, among those other than Lot and those of his people who believed in him. And His saying ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, ﴿and at night﴾ this is an address to the polytheists of Makkah, since they used to travel for trade to al-Sham and Palestine, and they pass by the Dead Sea, which is the place of the destroyed people of Lot; it became, after the sinking, a dead sea in which there is absolutely no life. His saying ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ is a rebuke and reproach to them for not reflecting and contemplating, for had they reflected they would have known that God Most High destroyed them because they denied their messenger and disbelieved in what he brought them of guidance and the true religion. These people have denied, so what prevents a punishment from befalling them as it befell the people of Lot before them?

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the prophethood and messengership of Lot.

2- Explanation of the lesson in the saving of Lot and the believers with him, and the destruction of the disbelievers who denied him.

3- Explanation that no intercession benefits, even if the intercessor is the closest of relatives, except after God permits the intercessor and is pleased with the one for whom intercession is made.

4- The obligation to reflect and reason upon cosmic events, so as to be guided thereby to knowledge of God's laws (sunan) in the universe and in life.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 139–148:

Explanation of the words:

﴿وإن يونس لمن المرسلين﴾: That is, and indeed Yunus ibn Matta, who is called Dhu al-Nun, is among the body of messengers.

﴿إذ أبق إلى الفلك المشحون﴾: That is, when he fled to the ship that was filled with passengers.

﴿فساهم فكان من المدحضين﴾: That is, he cast lots with the passengers of the ship, and he was among those who lost.

﴿فالتقمه الحوت وهو مليم﴾: That is, the fish swallowed him while he had come to deserve blame.

﴿للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون﴾: That is, the belly of the fish would have been a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿فنبذناه بالعراء﴾: That is, We cast him out into the belly of the fish, into the open, that is, onto the face of the earth, on the shore.

﴿وهو سقيم﴾: That is, ailing, like a featherless fledgling.

﴿شجرة من يقطين﴾: That is, the gourd (al-dubba'): the pumpkin.

﴿إلى مائة ألف أو يزيدون﴾: That is, We sent him to a hundred thousand souls, or more by some thousands.

﴿فآمنوا فمتعناهم إلى حين﴾: That is, his people believed when they saw the signs of the punishment, so God let them live until their appointed terms.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to mention those upon whom God bestowed favours in various forms. Thus the Exalted says, in continuation of what came before: ﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers﴾, that is, Our servant Yunus ibn Matta, Dhu al-Nun, was among those whom We favoured with prophethood and messengerhood. ﴿When he fled﴾, that is, at the time when he fled from his people because they did not believe in him, and he had promised them the punishment and it was delayed, so he grew impatient and fled from the city, which was Nineveh in the land of Mosul in Iraq. He reached the port and found a ship about to sail, so he boarded it. Its cargo was greater than its capacity, so it stood still in the midst of the sea, neither advancing nor retreating. The captain of the ship saw that it was necessary to reduce the load, or else everyone would drown, and each passenger was stingy with himself, so they cast lots, and Yunus was among those who lost (al-mudhdahin), that is, the defeated in the drawing of lots. They threw him into the sea, and the fish swallowed him, while he was ﴿blameworthy﴾, that is, doing what deserved blame by fleeing from calling his people to God when his chest was constricted and he could not bear to remain among them. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship, and he cast lots and was among the losers, and the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾.

And His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained in its belly﴾, that is, the belly of the fish, ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, the belly of the fish becoming a grave for him. That is, had Yunus not been among those who glorify God, that is, those who frequently pray, remember, supplicate and glorify God before the trial, he would not have been inspired to say, ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾, and his supplication would not have been answered. This is why the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Get to know God in ease and He will know you in hardship." The voice of Yunus was heard beneath the Throne, and some angels recognised it and mentioned that to their Lord, Exalted is He, and He informed them that it was His servant Yunus, who had been among those who frequently prayed, remembered and supplicated before the trial. Therefore God answered him and saved him from distress. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore﴾, that is, onto the bare surface of the earth, devoid of trees and of any shade, and he was like a featherless fledgling, his flesh cooked by the heat of the fish's belly. God caused a gourd plant to grow over him, that is, a branch that shaded him with its soft, silky leaves, on which flies do not settle. He also made a female wild goat ("ghazala") subservient to him, and it would come to him morning and evening, spread its legs for him and bring its udder near him, and he would suckle until he was satisfied, until he recovered his health and returned to his people, and found them believing, because of a repentance they had made when the signs of punishment appeared; so God accepted their repentance.

As for His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾, that is, We sent him to his people, who were the people of Nineveh, whose number was a hundred thousand and more by some thousands. They believed, that is, in God as Lord, in Islam as religion, and in Yunus as prophet and messenger, and they repented by abandoning polytheism and disbelief. So We rewarded them for their faith and repentance by removing from them the punishment that had overshadowed them, and ﴿We let them enjoy﴾, that is, We let them remain, enjoying life until the end of their appointed terms, which were determined for them in the Book of Decrees.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The affirmation of Yunus's prophethood and messengerhood, and within it the affirmation of the messengerhood of Muhammad ﷺ.

2- The permissibility of riding on sea vessels.

3- The permissibility of casting lots to settle disputes in dividing things and the like.

4- The virtue of prayer, remembrance, supplication and glorification of God, and their great benefit when one falls into trial.

5- The establishment of the principle "Get to know God in ease and He will know you in hardship."

6- The blessing of eating gourd, that is, the pumpkin, since the Prophet ﷺ used to eat it and pick it up from the edge of the dish.

7- The excellence of the people of Yunus, since they all believed, and no entire nation did so except them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 149–160:

Explanation of the words:

Fastaftihim (ask them): i.e., question the Meccan disbelievers in rebuke and reproach.

Wa lahum al-banun (and they have sons): i.e., so that they reserve for themselves the best and most noble.

Layaqulun walada Allah (they say, "Allah has begotten"): i.e., by their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah.

Istafa al-banat (He chose daughters): i.e., He chose daughters over sons.

Afala tadhakkarun (will you not reflect?): i.e., Allah, exalted be He, is free from any consort or offspring.

Am lakum sultan mubin (or do you have a clear authority?): i.e., do you have a clear proof for the correctness of what you claim?

Fa'tu bi-kitabikum (then bring your Book): i.e., the one in which you find support for your claims, and from where you have this.

Wa ja'alu baynahu wa bayn al-jinnah nasaba (and they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship): when they said the angels are the daughters of Allah.

Wa laqad 'alimat al-jinnah innahum lamuhdarun (but the jinn know that they will be brought forth [to punishment]): i.e., in the punishment.

Subhan Allah 'amma yasifun (Glory be to Allah above what they describe): i.e., exalting Allah above what they describe Him with, that the angels are His daughters.

Illa 'ibad Allah al-mukhlasin (except the sincere servants of Allah): i.e., they glorify their Lord and do not describe Him with deficiencies as these polytheists do.

Meaning of the verses:

After establishing, in the preceding context, the resurrection, the oneness of God, and prophethood by decisive proofs, arguments and evidences, Allah, exalted be He, intended to refute a slander that is among the worst slanders known in the land of the Arabian Peninsula, namely the saying of some of them that Allah has become related by marriage to the jinn and so begot the angels, who are His daughters. The answer is no; they did not witness their creation, so why do they lie? His saying, ﴿Verily, it is of their falsehood that they say, "Allah has begotten." And indeed they are liars,﴾ i.e., behold, these erring polytheists, out of their lie on which they have lived and to which they are accustomed, say "Allah has begotten," by their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah. What is wrong with you, how do you judge with this false and corrupt judgment? ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾, so that you would recall that Allah, exalted be He, is free from any consort or offspring. ﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾, i.e., do you have a strong proof establishing your claim? A strong proof comes by revelation from Allah in a Book He has sent down, declaring what you say. So then, ﴿bring your Book﴾ in which is what you claim, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your assertion.

And from where do you have a Book, when you have disbelieved in your Book which was sent down for your guidance, namely the noble Qur'an? Thus Allah refuted this slander with the strongest arguments. His saying, ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾, i.e., between Allah, exalted be He, and the jinn, by their saying that Allah has become related by marriage to the jinn and so married the noble women of the jinn; when Abu Bakr asked them, "Who are the mothers of the angels?", they said, "The noble women of the jinn." As for the Lord of everything, its Owner and Creator, reason does not accept that a consort or offspring be attributed to Him. Therefore, the servants of Allah whom He has selected for knowledge of Him, faith in Him and worship of Him do not describe their Lord, may His majesty be exalted, with attributes of created beings. And they will not be among those brought forth to the Fire.

Fa'tu bi-kitabikum (then bring your Book): i.e., the one in which you find support for your claims, and from where you have this.

Wa ja'alu baynahu wa bayn al-jinnah nasaba (and they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship): when they said the angels are the daughters of Allah.

Wa laqad 'alimat al-jinnah innahum lamuhdarun (but the jinn know that they will be brought forth [to punishment]): i.e., in the punishment.

Subhan Allah 'amma yasifun (Glory be to Allah above what they describe): i.e., exalting Allah above what they describe Him with, that the angels are His daughters.

Illa 'ibad Allah al-mukhlasin (except the sincere servants of Allah): i.e., they glorify their Lord and do not describe Him with deficiencies as these polytheists do.

Meaning of the verses:

After establishing, in the preceding context, the resurrection, the oneness of God, and prophethood by decisive proofs, arguments and evidences, Allah, exalted be He, intended to refute a slander that is among the worst slanders known in the land of the Arabian Peninsula, namely the saying of some of them that Allah has become related by marriage to the jinn and so begot the angels, who are His daughters. His saying, ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾, i.e., they were present on the day We created the angels, and thereby they would know that they were females. The answer is no; they did not witness their creation, so why do they lie? His saying, ﴿Verily, it is of their falsehood that they say, "Allah has begotten." And indeed they are liars,﴾ i.e., behold, these erring polytheists, out of their lie on which they have lived and to which they are accustomed, say "Allah has begotten," by their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah. And by the Lord of Might, they are indeed liars in this saying of theirs, which is an image of their falsehood by which they live. His saying, ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾ This is a rebuke and reproach to them: has Allah chosen daughters over sons, and therefore made them females as you claim? What is wrong with you, how do you judge with this false and corrupt judgment? ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾, so that you would recall that Allah, exalted be He, is free from any consort or offspring. ﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾, i.e., do you have a strong proof establishing your claim? A strong proof comes by revelation from Allah in a Book He has sent down, declaring what you say. So then, ﴿bring your Book﴾ in which is what you claim, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your assertion.

And from where do you have a Book, when you have disbelieved in your Book which was sent down for your guidance, namely the noble Qur'an? Thus Allah refuted this slander with the strongest arguments. His saying, ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾, i.e., between Allah, exalted be He, and the jinn, by their saying that Allah has become related by marriage to the jinn and so married the noble women of the jinn; when Abu Bakr asked them, "Who are the mothers of the angels?", they said, "The noble women of the jinn." His saying, ﴿But the jinn know that they will surely be brought forth [to punishment]﴾, i.e., in the punishment. How could they have a kinship with Him while Allah punishes them with the Fire? The kinsman honors his kinsman; he does not punish him with the Fire. By this, this detestable slander was refuted, and Allah, exalted be He, declared Himself free from such nonsense and falsehoods, saying, ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe.﴾ ﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah﴾, i.e., they do not describe their Lord with such deficiencies, which are attributes of weak servants who are in need of a spouse and offspring. As for the Lord of everything, its Owner and Creator, reason does not accept that a consort or offspring be attributed to Him. Therefore, the servants of Allah whom He has selected for knowledge of Him, faith in Him and worship of Him do not describe their Lord, may His majesty be exalted, with attributes of created beings. And they will not be among those brought forth to the Fire.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 37, verses 161–170:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa ma ta'buduna* (And what you worship): i.e., the idols.

*Illa man huwa sali al-jahim* (Except one who is destined to burn in the Fire): i.e., one for whom the punishment of the Fire has been decreed.

*Illa lahu maqam ma'lum* (Except that for him is a known station): i.e., a place in the heavens where Allah is worshipped, which he does not go beyond.

*Wa inna lanahnu as-saffun* (Indeed, we are those who line up): i.e., our feet in prayer.

*Wa inna lanahnu al-musabbihun* (And indeed, we are those who glorify): i.e., those who declare Allah free of whatever is unbefitting to Him.

*Wa in kanu la-yaqulun* (And indeed, they used to say): i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah.

*Law anna 'indana dhikran* (If we had with us a reminder): i.e., a Book from the books of the earlier nations.

*Fa kafaru bihi* (Yet they disbelieved in it): i.e., in the Book that came to them, which is the Qur'an.

*Fa sawfa ya'lamun* (But they will soon know): i.e., the consequence of their disbelief if they do not repent, believe and affirm the Oneness of Allah.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to refute the falsehood of the polytheists. Allah says to them, ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾ of idols, O polytheists. You cannot lead astray anyone except one who is destined to burn in the Fire, for We have written that in the Book of Decrees; he will inevitably act in a way that brings him the Fire. Such a person may be tempted by you and your worship, and so he goes astray by your misguidance. As for His saying, ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station. And indeed, we are the ones who line up. And indeed, we are the ones who glorify [Allah]﴾, this is the statement of Gabriel to the Prophet ﷺ, informing him that the angels line up in the heavens for prayer just as believers line up in prayer, and that they glorify Allah night and day. The Prophet ﷺ has informed us that there is no spot in the heavens the width of a palm but that an angel is upon it, either prostrating or standing. As for His saying, ﴿And indeed they used to say﴾, i.e., the polytheists of Arabia, ﴿If only we had with us a reminder from the former peoples﴾, i.e., a Book from the books of the earlier ones, such as the Torah and the Gospel, ﴿we would surely have been sincere servants of Allah﴾, i.e., we would have been servants of Allah who worship Him, affirm His Oneness, and do not associate anyone with Him. Allah responded to this claim of theirs, which is merely a false wish, by saying, ﴿Yet they disbelieved in it﴾, i.e., they disbelieved in the Book that came to them, which is the noble Qur'an. ﴿But they will soon know﴾ the consequence of their denial if they do not repent, which is their destruction and loss.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the doctrine of divine decree (al-qada' wa al-qadar), for whoever Allah has decreed the Fire for will surely burn in it.

2- Affirmation of the servitude of the angels and their obedience to Allah, and that they do not transgress the limits Allah has set for them.

3- The virtue of rows in prayer and the virtue of straightening them.

4- Exposing the lies of the polytheists, who used to claim that if a Book had been sent down to them as it was sent to those before them, they would have been sincere servants of Allah, i.e., those who worship Him and devote worship to Him alone.

5- Allah's warning to the polytheists for their lying, in His saying, ﴿But they will soon know﴾.
