**Explanation of the Words:**

**"Our word has preceded"**: this is His statement, exalted is He, "Indeed, My command has already preceded to My servants, the messengers."

**"And indeed, Our soldiers will surely be the victorious"**: that is, over the disbelievers, by proof and by help.

**"So turn away from them for a time"**: that is, withdraw from them until you are commanded to fight them.

**"And see them"**: that is, watch them.

**"And when it descends into their courtyard"**: that is, the punishment.

**"Turn away from them"**: that is, withdraw from them.

**"Glory be to your Lord"**: that is, exalting your Lord, O Muhammad.

**"Above what they describe"**: that is, exalting Him above what these polytheists attribute to Him of a consort, a son, and a partner.

**"And peace upon the messengers"**: that is, security from Allah for them in this world and the Hereafter.

**"And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds"**: that is, complete and sincere praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the two weights, mankind and the jinn, for His giving victory to His allies and destroying His enemies.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

When the first section was concluded with a warning to the disbelievers, in His words, "So they disbelieved in it, but they will soon know" [al-Saffat: 170], Allah, exalted is He, informed His Messenger with what would reassure him regarding Allah's victory for him. He said, "And已 indeed, Our word has preceded to Our servants, the messengers: indeed they are the ones who will be given victory, and indeed Our soldiers are the ones who will be victorious." That is, by proof and argument, and by spear and sword.

His statement, "So turn away from them for a time," commands His Messenger to withdraw from the polytheists of his people for a time, until He commands him concerning them with an order, or sends upon them a calamity or punishment. His statement, "And watch them," means: observe them, for they will surely see, without doubt, what will descend upon them of the punishment of Allah in this world and in the Hereafter.

His statement, exalted is He, "Will they then seek to hasten Our punishment?" [al-Saffat: 176] denounces their seeking to hasten the punishment, which shows their foolishness and lightness of intellect, for no one seeks to hasten punishment except a fool and an ignorant person. And the punishment they seek to hasten is the punishment of Allah!

He, exalted is He, said, "But when it descends into their courtyard," that is, into the courtyard of their dwellings, "then evil is the morning of those who were warned," that is, wretched is their morning, a morning of their destruction and annihilation.

Then Allah, exalted is He, again commanded His Messenger to turn away from them and await what will befall them, saying, "So turn away from them for a time, and watch, for they will [soon] see." In this verse there is a threat and warning to these polytheists beyond measure.

Finally, Allah, exalted is He, exalted Himself above what the polytheists attribute to Him of a son and a partner, sent peace upon the messengers, and praised Himself, pointing to what praise requires and necessitates, which is that He is the Lord of the worlds. So He said, "Glory be to your Lord," O Muhammad, "the Lord of might," and its Owner, who grants might to whom He wills and humbles whom He wills, "above what they describe" of a consort, a son, and a partner. "And peace" from Us "upon the messengers," and you are among them. "And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds," for His giving victory to His allies and destroying His enemies.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. Affirmation of Muhammad's prophethood.
2. Allah's promise to His Messenger of victory, which He has fulfilled, and praise belongs to Allah.
3. The recommendation of concluding a supplication or speech by reciting the sentence, "Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe. And peace upon the messengers. And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds," because this is reported in the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition).

**Explanation of the Words:**

**"Our word has preceded"**: this is His statement, exalted is He, "Indeed, My command has already preceded to My servants, the messengers."

**"And indeed, Our soldiers will surely be the victorious"**: that is, over the disbelievers, by proof and by help.

**"So turn away from them for a time"**: that is, withdraw from them until you are commanded to fight them.

**"And see them"**: that is, watch them.

**"And when it descends into their courtyard"**: that is, the punishment.

**"Turn away from them"**: that is, withdraw from them.

**"Glory be to your Lord"**: that is, exalting your Lord, O Muhammad.

**"Above what they describe"**: that is, exalting Him above what these polytheists attribute to Him of a consort, a son, and a partner.

**"And peace upon the messengers"**: that is, security from Allah for them in this world and the Hereafter.

**"And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds"**: that is, complete and sincere praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the two weights, mankind and the jinn, for His giving victory to His allies and destroying His enemies.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

When the first section was concluded with a warning to the disbelievers, in His words, "So they disbelieved in it, but they will soon know" [al-Saffat: 170], Allah, exalted is He, informed His Messenger with what would reassure him regarding Allah's victory for him. He said, "And已 indeed, Our word has preceded to Our servants, the messengers: indeed they are the ones who will be given victory, and indeed Our soldiers are the ones who will be victorious." That is, by proof and argument, and by spear and sword.

His statement, "So turn away from them for a time," commands His Messenger to withdraw from the polytheists of his people for a time, until He commands him concerning them with an order, or sends upon them a calamity or punishment. His statement, "And watch them," means: observe them, for they will surely see, without doubt, what will descend upon them of the punishment of Allah in this world and in the Hereafter.

His statement, exalted is He, "Will they then seek to hasten Our punishment?" [al-Saffat: 176] denounces their seeking to hasten the punishment, which shows their foolishness and lightness of intellect, for no one seeks to hasten punishment except a fool and an ignorant person. And the punishment they seek to hasten is the punishment of Allah!

He, exalted is He, said, "But when it descends into their courtyard," that is, into the courtyard of their dwellings, "then evil is the morning of those who were warned," that is, wretched is their morning, a morning of their destruction and annihilation.

Then Allah, exalted is He, again commanded His Messenger to turn away from them and await what will befall them, saying, "So turn away from them for a time, and watch, for they will [soon] see." In this verse there is a threat and warning to these polytheists beyond measure.

Finally, Allah, exalted is He, exalted Himself above what the polytheists attribute to Him of a son and a partner, sent peace upon the messengers, and praised Himself, pointing to what praise requires and necessitates, which is that He is the Lord of the worlds. So He said, "Glory be to your Lord," O Muhammad, "the Lord of might," and its Owner, who grants might to whom He wills and humbles whom He wills, "above what they describe" of a consort, a son, and a partner. "And peace" from Us "upon the messengers," and you are among them. "And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds," for His giving victory to His allies and destroying His enemies.
